newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Police raid Hanbo to seize documents.
newsitem.headline: Police raid Hanbo to seize documents.

text.p: South Korean police raided offices of the troubled Hanbo Group on Tuesday following allegations of misconduct in a loan scandal centred on the company's failed steel unit, state radio said.
On Monday, President Kim Young-sam ordered a thorough investigation into South Korea's 14th largest industrial conglomerate.
The Korea Broadcasting System said police were looking for loan-related documents. State prosecutors were not immediately available for comment.
Finance ministry officials say Hanbo borrowed about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) from banks and financial institutions, about 20 times its net worth.
Opposition parties say the loans to Hanbo Steel Co, the group's flagship, would not have been possible without government influence-peddling.
Hanbo Steel defaulted on debt last week and is seeking court protection with three other group units.
